Fig. 7
Synthesis of a dipeptide from two amino acids (AAs). R1 and R2 represent the side chains of the two AAs. With the loss of one H2O
molecule (one “H” atom from the a-amino group of an AA and the “-OH” from the carboxyl group of the other AA), a peptide bond (-CONH-) is
formed. This reaction is used to produce peptides through chemical manufacturing, and is catalyzed by enzymes in human cells. Peptides are
generally stable in an aqueous solution.
